basis: CSX first established the decline when it released Q1 2025 results on April 16. Its consolidated GAAP income statement reports $3,423 million of revenue for the quarter ended March 31, 2025 and $3,681 million for the quarter ended March 31, 2024. The 95% cutoff was $3,496.95 million, so actual revenue was $73.95 million below it. The full February 19 Barclays transcript resolves the disagreement between the earlier reviews. Management’s $350 million estimate covered full-year pressures including costs. Its 3% Q1 decline forecast applied to sequential coal yield. Neither figure set an upper bound for consolidated quarterly revenue.

coverage.detail: October 16, 2024, preceding earnings cycle. CSX expected a moderate revenue decline in Q4 2024, with about $200 million of pressure from fuel and coal markets. The outlook covered the December quarter.
November 7 Investor Day. The mid-single-digit revenue growth target was a compound annual rate from 2024 to 2027. It supplied no Q1 2025 endpoint.
November 12 Exhibit 99.1 announced a change in legal leadership effective in January.
November 13 Baird conference. CFO Sean Pelkey discussed three-year earnings growth and identified domestic coal and network pressures for 2025 without quantifying consolidated Q1 revenue.
November 19 Stephens conference. Management discussed Q4 freight volumes and the duration of Blue Ridge rerouting. It deferred the 2025 outlook to January.
December 4 UBS conference. Management discussed multi-year growth targets, commodity markets and 2025 network disruption without giving a consolidated Q1 revenue ceiling.
January 23, 2025, previous earnings release. The $3.54 billion of revenue and 4% year-over-year decline were Q4 2024 actuals. The release supplied no numeric Q1 2025 revenue forecast.

January 23 earnings presentation and call. Low- to mid-single-digit growth referred to full-year freight volume. Management identified Q1 as the likely operating-income trough. The roughly 3% sequential Q1 decline referred to coal revenue per unit. [Call transcript](https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/csx/transcripts/242218-q4-2024/)
January 27 Exhibit 99.1 announced Ann Begeman’s appointment to the board.

CSX’s February 11 notice identifies CEO Joe Hinrichs and CFO Sean Pelkey as the speakers for the public February 19 Barclays webcast at 8:40 a.m. ET. The issuer’s past-events page yielded no readable 2025 replay. [Issuer event archive](https://investors.csx.com/news-and-events/events-and-presentations/default.aspx?ShowEvents=PAST)

The Barclays-hosted agenda found in the search lists CSX but dates the meeting to February 23–24, 2022. The prior review’s 2025 transcript preview stopped at the opening question. [Preview](https://seekingalpha.com/article/4759753-csx-corporation-csx-barclays-42nd-annual-industrial-select-conference-transcript)

February 19 gap resolved. The Quartr transcript on Stock Analysis includes management’s answers through the closing exchange. Pelkey placed the approximately $350 million headwind over the full year, concentrated in the first half and including rerouting costs. Asked specifically about Q1 coal yield, he confirmed a 3% decline from Q4. The session supplied no numeric consolidated Q1 revenue ceiling.

March 7 and 10 Forms 8-K. The $600 million was principal on notes due in 2035. The filings documented the underwriting agreement and completion of the offering. [March 10 filing](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/277948/000119312525050848/d940299d8k.htm)

March 11 J.P. Morgan conference. CSX’s eight-page deck compared January and February daily freight volumes with Q4 averages. Pelkey retained the full-year volume outlook and identified approximately $10 million per month of disruption costs within the $350 million headwind. He gave no consolidated Q1 revenue endpoint. [Conference transcript](https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/csx/transcripts/325470-j-p-morgan-industrials-conference-2025/)

March 19. CSX scheduled results for after market close on April 16 without giving a preliminary figure. Its intervening March 25 and April 14 announcements concerned labor agreements and safety awards. [Issuer press archive](https://www.csx.com/index.cfm/about-us/media/press-releases/?nextNID=65F0F4D9-EE2E-1998-C9D28CFDB55CA69C&startRow=51)

April 16 Exhibit 99.2 reports both March quarters on the same consolidated revenue row, including trucking in both periods. The $258 million decrease rounds to 7%. Exhibit 99.1 independently gives the rounded $3.42 billion and 7% decline. [Earnings release](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/277948/000027794825000027/pressrelease_q12025.htm)

publication_date_evidence: CSX datelined its public earnings announcement April 16, 2025. EDGAR accepted the Item 2.02 Form 8-K containing the release and quarterly financial statements that day at 16:01:28, before the scheduled 4:30 p.m. ET call. [CSX announcement](https://www.csx.com/index.cfm/about-us/media/press-releases/csx-corp-announces-first-quarter-2025-results/) [SEC acceptance record](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/277948/000027794825000027/0000277948-25-000027-index.htm)
